assessment.calibration_basis: p_engine is 0.90, driven by the scorecard's anonymous-proxy device-ring floor adjustment (+0.90) that overrides the low model-based cms_p (0.0713) and cal_p (0.0797); the ring floor applies because the flagged transaction sits on a strong profile (is_strong=true) behind IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS with 52 cards all-time / 28 cards in the 30 days before opening and 4 closed cases already confirmed as undocumented fraud on this exact profile. I kept the probability at the engine value (within the ±0.10 band) because two independent evidence families — device/ring (device_neighbors, ring_profile) and case memory (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, CC-3035) — both point the same direction and satisfy the §6 stop condition; the low cms_p/risk_score reflects the model not recognising the proxy-ring shape, not a legitimacy signal strong enough to move off the floor.

evidence.claim: Four closed cases already confirmed the same device profile as undocumented fraud between August and September 2016: CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985 and CC-3035, all with a report filed.

Card C13487-K1's own activity on this ring profile before opening consists of two online, product-code-C purchases: 3460634 ($112.37, 2016-11-15 20:30) and the flagged 3478561 ($74.96, 2016-11-22 16:11), both marked device_new=New and routed through IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS.

The flagged amount of $74.96 sits inside the card's baseline of 71 prior transactions (prior median $55.92, prior maximum $225.94), and the case-memory calibration (cms_p 0.071, real-time risk_score 0.05) is low on its own, but this reading is outweighed by the two independent ring/memory evidence families above.
The online billing region 191.0 is one of only two regions the card uses (36 prior purchases there over 34 distinct days, hint=known), so the region itself is not a novelty signal for this card.
The customer has a single card on file (n_cards=1) and no prior closed or agent cases, so this device-ring exposure is the first and only fraud signal on the account.

assessment.pattern_description: Anonymous-proxy device ring: the strong device profile `SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080`, always seen behind `IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS`, is shared by 52 cards all-time and 28 cards in the 30 days before this case opened, with 19 of those cards already active on the profile pre-open and 27 in the current wave. It affects many different customers' cards making small online purchases flagged as a New device on each account. The pattern was found by following the flagged transaction to its device profile via case_context/ring_profile and out to the other cards on that profile via device_neighbors, and is corroborated by four closed cases (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, CC-3035) that the bank already confirmed as this same undocumented fraud shape in August-September.

actions.reason: 3a: verdict fraud with probability 0.90 and the pattern is undocumented (anonymous-proxy device ring), so a case is opened to record the evidence.

R6: the shared device profile SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080 behind IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS connects this card to 27 other cards in the current wave, so every sharing card is recommended for monitoring.
§3b: fraud verdict on a shared anonymous-proxy device ring with exposure $187.33 ≤ $2,500, so blocking this card is recommended to L1 rather than executed automatically.

3a/R6: exposure is under $1,000 but the case connects to a shared device profile and to another card's confirmed fraud (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, CC-3035 on the same profile), so a report is recommended to L2.
R9: the ring shows coordinated, repeated abuse across many customers' cards on one device profile, an undocumented pattern that the analyst should review further.
